design:
D1. Mostly a measurement; the only code is the drive. H adds no Hub behaviour: builds, levels, budgets and landing targets are slice D's, batching E's, the views F's and G's, the check order L's, the override M's, the mender N's. The drive (scripts/drive/measured_rerun_check.py) is the acceptance check: GET requests only, so it is safe on :8000, and it fails on today's master because no build has a level and G's views do not exist.

D2. The candidate is F1013+F1014+F1015, bundled as 'Every same-file overlap reaches the operator'. All three are open, Ready, Tier 0, with named repro tests, and their causes still hold on master bbf3f10: spec_completeness.py:418-429 (_normalise_path only swaps backslashes; paths_overlap compares strings), spec_payload.py:564-576 (no '..' refusal), spec_service.py:1962 (phase_findings adds overlap_warnings but not undeclared_files_warnings, which only the save carries at :420-421), SpecPhaseParts.tsx:21-32 (GapLines prints group[0].message). Three tasks across Python and UI exercise L's UI check, the reviewer and the merge queue, and are small enough to pay for twice. Slices C and F touch the same surfaces (propose becomes Check; F rewrites hub/ui/src/components/spec), so task 1 re-confirms the repros on the base commit and falls back to the next qualifying finding set if they moved.

D3. Same driver at both levels (the Hub's flow). Both baselines were flows, and holding the driver fixed means the comparison isolates the level. A lead-driven build is a separate question (open question 1).

D4. Sequential, Fast first, on a quiet machine. Concurrent builds would contend for CPU, and on 2026-10-25 load made check runs slow and timing tests flake (src-17aeb9aea81f:64-68). Order matters little since each starts from the same base on its own branch; Fast first gives the cheaper result early if the budget runs out.

D5. Off master. Each build lands on its own branch (D's landing target). That removes the restart and live-bundle hazards and lets the two results be compared side by side. Merging the chosen result is the operator's decision, made after the note is recorded.

D6. Budget and stop rule. The cap per build is $30 API-equivalent, window 8 h, $65 for the whole measurement including one re-run. Baselines: $52 for 6 tasks over 7 h 26 min (src-17aeb9aea81f:17-22); $44 for 4 tasks over 6 h 47 min (2026-10-26/27). Three tasks at the night's rate of about $11 each fit under $30 at Gated. A build that hits its cap is itself a result, so it is recorded, not rescued. A Hub defect that blocks a build for 30 min measures the defect, not the level, so the build stops, the defect is filed, and both builds are re-run once.

D7. Defects are classified by hand, with reasons. The views can list send-backs and check failures (K's per-piece reasons, task_check_runs results), but whether a failure was the change's, a flake or the Hub's needs judgement. Escaped defects are measured by running every check and the candidate's criteria on each landing branch, run by an agent outside both builds.

D8. Views first, queries marked. Numbers are read from G's project view and F's build panel. When a number is missing, the gap is filed against the view rather than worked around silently. The underlying records outlive the measurement: runs, outputs and events are never pruned (trace_retention.py:17), while traces are kept 14 days (:39), so nothing H reads depends on traces. The baselines are re-read from the views as soon as G ships, as a check on G's totals.

D9. The re-recording rule is decided here, not left to taste. Carry forward only when at least 5 re-judged held pieces all held and their review rounds cost at least 10% of all review. One that failed means re-recording caught a regression, and carry-forward would have hidden it. The cost is an upper bound: the whole review round after a send-back that held pieces, because per-tool-call cost is not recorded (turn_usage is per run, models.py:1570-1587).

D10. Vault recording. The note is a file under .agentweave/vault-notes/ (where the 2026-10-26 retrospective lives), added through the operator's POST /vault/paths (api/v1/vault.py:330-346; type 'document', the default at :264; distil true). A tracked source is written to knowledge/sources/<id>.md then <id>.json (vault.py:76, :936-937) and committed. It is not a 'decision' source, because decisions are never distilled (api/v1/vault.py:204-205).

lifecycle: Tier 2 (hazard): two paid builds on the operator's live :8000 Hub and project, whose landing on master would put Hub and UI code into the checkout :8000 runs and the bundle its app loads. One-off: a measurement recorded in the vault, folding into no capability; its drive stays in scripts/drive/.

open_questions.question: Should a third build be added, Fast driven by a lead agent (the retrospective's first recommendation), under its own $30 cap? Default here: no; both builds use the Hub's flow, so the level is the only thing that differs. Decided 2026-10-27 (orchestrator, under the operator's authority): no third build; the lead driver is exercised by slice D's own acceptance drive.

Which change is measured: F1013+F1014+F1015 as 'Every same-file overlap reaches the operator', or the next qualifying open finding set if they no longer reproduce on the base commit (decided, design D2).
Which result reaches master: the operator chooses after reading the comparison; the other landing branch is deleted once the note is recorded (decided, design D5).

problem: Two nights of flows produced the numbers this roadmap answers, both found by SQL. 2026-10-25: 6 tasks, 7 h 26 min and not finished, 48 runs, 16 check-gate runs (~147 min), 9 send-backs of which about half were caused by the Hub, 4 real defects caught by QA, about $52 (src-17aeb9aea81f:17-22, :35-42). 2026-10-26/27, slice B: 4 tasks, 6 h 47 min, about $44, the mender 36% of it (42 Opus runs, $15.9). Every send-back was something a check catches (24 UI test failures, a surface ceiling, ruff). Three reviews ran beside checks that had already failed (~52 min, ~$4.4). A test failing on main too held an approved task for 2 h 40 min, and 27 mender questions expired. The retrospective ends: re-run a slice-sized job and compare wall time and real defects caught; that comparison is the evidence for keeping AgentWeave (src-17aeb9aea81f:156-159). Separately, carrying held evidence forward was deferred until this measurement says what re-recording costs (roadmap non-goal; slice K non-goal). Today no view shows a flow's cost or time: a grep of hub/hub/api for GET routes on stats, usage, cost or spend finds none.

requirements.rationale: It must touch the UI so slice L's UI check can fire, be small enough to pay for twice, and have defects a reviewer or a check can find; three Ready Tier 0 findings on one seam fit.
requirements.statement: The change built for the measurement is one change document of two to four tasks that edits both hub/hub and hub/ui, whose findings are open and whose repro tests fail on the base commit. The candidate is F1013, F1014 and F1015 bundled as 'Every same-file overlap reaches the operator' (spec/changes/every-same-file-overlap-reaches-the-operator/spec.json); if any of the three no longer reproduces on the base commit, the next open, Ready finding set meeting the same rule is used and the comparison says why.

requirements.rationale: Only the level may differ, or the comparison cannot say what the level bought.
requirements.statement: Both builds start from the same main commit and use the same driver (the Hub's flow), the same builder agents bound to the same runners and models, the same mender model and the same project checks; the reviewer exists only at Gated. Each build's record, as the app shows it, names its base commit, level, builders and the model of every run.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-10-25 machine load made timing tests flake and check runs slow (src-17aeb9aea81f section 2.9); concurrent builds would measure each other.
requirements.statement: The two builds run one after the other, Fast first, while no other flow or build runs in the project, no agent is building other work, and no leftover Hub or test process from an earlier drive is running on the machine.

requirements.rationale: :8000 runs this checkout, so master is what it executes at its next restart, and a committed UI bundle reaches the operator's live app on its next reload (CLAUDE.md, The Hubs on this machine).
requirements.statement: Each build lands its approved work on its own branch cut from the base commit, never on master; no commit of either build reaches master until the operator chooses, after the comparison is recorded, which result to merge.

requirements.rationale: The baselines cost about $52 for 6 tasks and $44 for 4; a measurement that keeps paying to rescue itself measures the rescue.
requirements.statement: Each build runs under a budget cap of $30 API-equivalent and a window of 8 hours, and stops at either; a stopped build is recorded with its numbers as they stood and marked stopped, never restarted. If a build is blocked for over 30 minutes by a Hub defect rather than the change, it is stopped, a finding is filed, and both builds are re-run once after the fix from a common new base; a second such stop, or the measurement's total passing $65, ends it as inconclusive with what it found.

The comparison has four columns: the 2026-10-25 flow (loop-df5f74816122), the night of 2026-10-26/27 (slice B's flow), the Fast build and the Gated build. For each it gives tasks; wall time in total and per task, split into building, waiting for review, checks and waiting to be handed out; API-equivalent cost in total, per task and by role (building, reviewing, mender); send-backs; real defects caught, each with where it was caught (check, reviewer, operator); escaped defects; and operator actions during the build.

requirements.rationale: These are what slices L, M and N exist to remove; on 2026-10-26/27 they were three reviews and about $4.4, 2 h 40 min, 42 Opus runs and $15.9, 6 loop_stalled wakes, and 27 questions.
requirements.statement: For each column the comparison also gives: review turns that started while the task's latest check run had failed, with their minutes and cost; hours a task's approval waited on a failure that was not the task's; mender turns, mender cost and the mender's model; mender wakes with no stalled work behind them; and mender questions that expired unanswered.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-10-25 about half the send-backs were caused by the Hub (src-17aeb9aea81f section 2.3); counting them as caught defects would credit the gate for its own failures.
requirements.statement: Every send-back and every failed check run in the Fast and Gated columns is listed with a link to its task and classified as a defect in the change, a failure that was not the task's (fails on main too, or passes on a serial rerun), or a Hub defect, with a one-line reason; only the first kind counts as a real defect caught.

requirements.rationale: Fast is only cheaper if it does not ship what Gated catches; without this the comparison rewards skipping review.
requirements.statement: After each build ends, the candidate's acceptance criteria and every project check, the UI check included, are run on that build's landed branch by someone who took no part in the build, and each failure is counted as an escaped defect of that build.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done line for this slice; and on 2026-10-25 finding where the time went took SQL against the operator's database (src-17aeb9aea81f section 2.12).
requirements.statement: Every number in the Fast and Gated columns, and in the baseline columns wherever the views cover those flows, is read from the app's own views (slice G's project view and the spec page's build panel), and the comparison names the view each number came from. Wall time, cost and real defects for Fast and Gated come from a view; any other number no view shows is filed as a finding against that view and given from a read-only query, marked as such.

requirements.rationale: Carrying forward was deferred until this measurement (roadmap non-goal; slice K non-goal). A re-recorded piece that fails is a regression the carry-forward would have hidden.
requirements.statement: The comparison measures re-recording held evidence over every send-back in the project since slice K shipped, the Gated build's included: held pieces recorded again, the review rounds that judged them again with their minutes and cost, and how many failed when judged again. It ends with a recommendation by this rule: carry held pieces forward when at least 5 were judged again, none failed, and those review rounds cost at least 10% of all review cost; keep re-recording when any failed; otherwise keep re-recording and say the evidence is too thin.

The comparison is one Markdown note added to the project's tracked vault as a 'document' source, dated the day it was written and distilled, so that it is listed in the Vault tab, its body and metadata are committed under knowledge/sources/, and its facts can be cited by the document that decides carrying forward.

in_scope: Choosing the measured change and confirming its findings reproduce on the base commit
One Fast and one Gated build of it on :8000, same base, driver, builders and models, landing off master
A budget cap, a window and a stop rule for the measurement
Checking each build's result for escaped defects
A four-column comparison (2026-10-25, 2026-10-26/27, Fast, Gated), with the L/M/N effect rows
The cost of re-recording held evidence, and a recommendation on carrying it forward
Recording the comparison in the tracked vault, with gaps in the views filed as findings
An acceptance drive that checks the comparison against the app's routes
non_goals: Building carry-forward of held evidence: if recommended, it becomes its own change
A Reviewed-level build, or a lead-driven build: unless the operator answers open question 1
Comparing AgentWeave with Claude Code subagents: those runs leave no turn_usage in the Hub, so no view can show them
New views or stats: slices F and G own them; H files what they lack
Merging either build to master: the operator's choice, after the note
Fixing what the builds find in the Hub: filed as findings, built by their own changes

summary: Closes the roadmap by measuring it. One slice-sized change, F1013-F1015 bundled as 'Every same-file overlap reaches the operator', is built twice on the operator's Hub from the same base commit, with the same builders and models: once at Fast, once at Gated, one after the other, each landing on its own branch off master, each under a $30 cap and an 8-hour window. The comparison sets them beside the 2026-10-25 responsiveness flow and slice B's flow of 2026-10-26/27 on wall time, cost, real defects caught, escaped defects, and what slices L, M and N were built to remove: reviews of already-failed checks, approvals held by failures that were not the task's, and the mender's turns. It also measures what re-recording held evidence costs and recommends whether to carry it forward. Every number is read from the app's own views, and the comparison is recorded in the vault.
